items.stem: A teammate should be able to leave feedback on a document but must not change its contents. Which Drive access level fits?

options.rationale: Correct: commenter allows comments and suggestions but not edits.
Editor can change the contents, which is not wanted here.
Owner has full control including deletion and sharing.
No access would prevent leaving feedback entirely.

items.explanation: Correct: commenter allows comments and suggestions but not edits.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support good collaboration in Google Docs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use suggesting mode when reviewing someone else's draft
options.rationale: Correct: suggestions let the author accept or reject changes.

options.text: Use comments to raise questions without altering the text
options.rationale: Correct: comments keep feedback separate from content.

options.text: Overwrite the author's text directly during review
options.rationale: Direct edits during review lose the author's control.

options.text: Delete version history to keep the document tidy
options.rationale: Version history is valuable and should be preserved.

items.explanation: Correct: suggesting mode and comments keep review non-destructive.

items.stem: You collect event sign-ups with Google Forms and want responses to update automatically for analysis. What should you do?

options.text: Link the Form's responses to a Google Sheet
options.rationale: Correct: linking responses to a Sheet lets them populate automatically for analysis.

options.text: Copy each response into a Doc by hand
options.rationale: Manual copying is error-prone and not automatic.

options.text: Export a PDF after every response
options.rationale: PDFs are static and not suited to ongoing analysis.

options.text: Email yourself each submission and retype it
options.rationale: Retyping is manual and defeats automation.

items.explanation: Correct: linking responses to a Sheet lets them populate automatically for analysis.
